prompts.question_guidance:
Before you ask, look for the answer in the specifications, the code and the map, and ask only what they leave open. Ask only about a decision that cannot easily be undone. A choice that can be undone is yours: make it, write it and its reason on the ticket, and carry on.
The user reads your question on the map with none of your context: say what it is about and why it needs deciding, in plain words, without your own labels or ids. Each suggested answer says what it leads to.
prompts.question_form:
Before asking, look for the answer in the specifications, code and map. Work never stops for a question. Ask only about a decision that is not easily reversed. Make a reversible choice yourself, write the choice and its reason on the ticket, and carry on. Build a real fork that changes behavior significantly and has tradeoffs behind a setting with a sensible default; record the setting, its default and the reason on the ticket. A small choice of style or wording is reversible, not a setting.
Fill every part of this form:
#1 Specifications reviewed: List the specification files you read and explain what they leave undecided. Submit this as specs=.
#2 Why this is not a configuration option: Explain why the decision is not easily reversed and why it cannot be handled as a behavior fork behind a setting with a sensible default. Submit this as not_option=.
#3 Unexplained "Rich said": If an unexplained statement is the blocker, give its exact words and where it appears. Otherwise say "None; the decision and its reason are described in the question." Submit this as rich_said=.
#4 Question and suggested answers: Write for a person who has not read your context. Say what you were doing, what you found, why a decision is needed, the choices, what each means and leads to, and which you recommend. Use plain words without relying on your own labels or ids. Each suggested answer says what it leads to; put the recommended answer first. These become buttons on the map. Submit the question and suggestions=, identify who asks with by=, and link the ticket with work=.
How to submit: metaform map ask <node> "<your question>" specs="<files reviewed and what remains undecided>" not_option="<why not easily reversed or configurable>" rich_said="<exact words and source, or none>" suggestions='["<recommended choice and its consequence>", "<another choice and its consequence>"]' by="<your agent and ticket>" work=<work id>.
Record what depends on the answer on the ticket and carry on with work that does not depend on it. Submitting a question does not end your turn. If no work remains that you can continue, end your turn with the ticket incomplete so the next ticket can start. If you receive the answer another way, record it with metaform map reply <id> answer="..." so the question closes and the node stops glowing.
prompts.question_thanks: Your question is recorded at the node. Record what depends on the answer on the ticket and carry on with work that does not depend on it. If no work remains that you can continue, end your turn with the ticket incomplete so the next ticket can start.
prompts.blind_spot_challenge:
<instructions> BLIND SPOT CHALLENGE
MODE A: FAST MODE
Please do not examine the code for your report. You may have access to the project folder, but use it only to read the specifications, so you can answer questions about what you can observe in the functional diagram.
We want you to be a fresh set of eyes looking in on the project. As you review the design, surface anything you think we are overlooking.
MODE B: CRITIC MODE
You have full access to the map, our specifications, and our code. If you are performing this challenge, we are probably in the middle of construction. Since you can see our code, examine recently completed tasks, our specifications, and anything else that helps you see the big picture.
If something in the code looks wrong, write up a few tickets for us as you go. That is a big help.
Remember: you are looking for oversights, not work we simply haven't gotten to yet.
BOTH MODES
We have one request: make your suggestions valuable and substantial, the kind you can make a case for. Tell us how and why each suggestion will make our project better.
If you don't take this seriously, we are wasting each other's time. Good luck. We hope you find a big, substantial blind spot! </instructions>
